correctness.rationale: A failure occurs at some x precisely when Q=↓x∩¬A is covered by B∪C but by neither alone. Hence Q has distinct incomparable maxima u,v, and x has an A-predecessor. A minimal such predecessor s is minimal in P and incomparable with both u and v. The downsets Q without u and ↓u cover Q properly; independently adjoining s to either and reversing the ordered pair gives eight distinct failures with the same A. The induced poset on s,u,v,x is A_3⊕A_1; restriction of downsets is onto its nine-element lattice, and equality of sizes makes restriction an isomorphism. In this poset three singleton antecedents each give eight failures, verified directly over 9^3 ordered triples. In the displayed size-h family the base fork plus an isolated s has ten downsets, and each upper-chain point adds exactly one. Only A={s} can fail, only at an upper-chain witness; then u and v must be assigned to opposite consequents, with independent choices for including s, giving exactly eight for each h≥11. Direct implication over 11^3 triples also confirms the seed count. These finite checks corroborate the multiplicities rather than replace the universal proof.
residual_risks: The record leaves the size-ten optimum open. Counts are over ordered triples and do not concern admissibility of the KP rule.

evidence: Downsets of P are upsets on the opposite Kripke frame. The four-point P-obstruction is a root under three incomparable terminal points in that orientation.
